name: the-cellular-interface-multicellular
title: The Cellular Interface, Multicellular
lead:
This is the spatial, multicellular-capable counterpart to `draft-to-living-cell`: the same
nine interface-composition patterns from the paper, realized this time as real 2D spatial
frameworks — chiefly a Cellular Potts Model (viva-cpm) coupled to spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes — rather than lumped ODEs and scripted events.
Where `draft-to-living-cell` asked "can this pattern be authored as an inert typed draft and
compiled into a runnable mechanism," this investigation asks "does the pattern survive when
the mechanism is a real spatial simulator built by someone else, composed in through one typed
interface." The flagship, `cell-environment-coupling-spatial`, builds and runs exactly one such
composition: `CpmCellField`, a process that reads a spatio-flux nutrient grid at a CPM cell's
own footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA step there (`e_coli_core`, oxygen-capped to force acetate
overflow), grows the cell's CPM target volume from the biomass produced, and writes the
uptake/secretion back into the shared field as a spatial delta that spatio-flux's
`DiffusionAdvection` then spreads. Over 20 ticks the cell grows roughly 3.4x (32 to 110 CPM
lattice pixels, on a 60x60 = 3600-pixel field — it does not come close to filling the lattice),
depletes the glucose at its own footprint by up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies
it, and secretes a spreading acetate plume — niche construction made spatially and
metabolically real, not scripted. Three more studies are built and run alongside the flagship —
cell-cell coupling (multi-cell field competition), disintegration (structural-integrity
release), and growth-and-division. The remaining five (the cellular-interface contract itself,
molecular-scale reaction-diffusion, sorting and phase separation, a self-maintained protocell,
and colony development) are planned or in progress, not yet built; this file is honest about
that.

at_a_glance.role:
The flagship (spatial Fig 5) — a real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient
field through one typed process (`CpmCellField`): senses local glucose, runs dynamic-FBA
(e_coli_core, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows (~3.4x CPM volume), and secretes a
diffusing acetate plume. Niche construction as genuine spatial-metabolic output, not a
scripted trajectory.

how_to_read:
Four studies exist so far: `cell-environment-coupling-spatial` (the flagship),
`cell-cell-coupling-spatial`, `disintegration-spatial`, and `growth-and-division-spatial`. Read
each alongside its specification-stage analogue in `draft-to-living-cell` for the same
interface claim at two mechanistic resolutions — lumped 1-D/ODE there, real 2D CPM+spatio-flux
here. The design spec
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-cellular-interface-multicellular-design.md`) lays out the
remaining planned studies and the increment order they are expected to land in.

glossary.definition: A lattice-based cell-shape simulation framework (here, viva-cpm, a Rust-backed engine) in which cells occupy sets of pixels and evolve their shape, adhesion, and volume by energy-minimizing Monte Carlo pixel copies, rather than being represented as a scalar state bundle.
A process-bigraph-native package providing spatial reaction-diffusion-advection PDE processes (`DiffusionAdvection`) and spatial dynamic flux-balance analysis (`DynamicFBA`) over a 2D field grid.

The coupling process this investigation's flagship builds: a process-bigraph Process that owns a viva-cpm world object, reads a shared spatio-flux `fields` grid at the CPM cell's current footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA step there, grows the CPM cell's target volume from the resulting biomass, and writes the uptake/secretion back into the field as a spatial delta. The typed interface the paper's composition claim is made concrete through.
The cell measurably reshaping the very environmental gradient it depends on — here, the CPM cell's footprint measurably depleting the local glucose field before diffusion partially resupplies it.

Plausible, hand-tuned constants (e.g. glucose_km, glucose_vmax, oxygen_vmax, box_volume_L, grow_per_biomass) chosen to produce legible, gradual dynamics over a short run — not fitted to a named organism, medium, or literature target.

A study in this investigation that realizes the same composition pattern as a named study in draft-to-living-cell, but with real 2D spatial frameworks (CPM, spatio-flux, and future reaction-diffusion/phase-field processes) instead of lumped ODEs and scripted events.

biological_story:
A cell in a real 2D environment is not a point that reads and writes scalars —
it is a shape, occupying a footprint of lattice pixels that grows, moves, and metabolizes at
whatever concentration happens to sit under it right now. `draft-to-living-cell`'s Fig 5 study
showed that sensing and acting are one coupling over a shared field, not two separate
subsystems, using a lumped 9-cell 1-D grid and a scripted-shape cell. This investigation asks
the same question with the scripting removed: can a genuine Cellular Potts Model cell, built
and validated as its own independent simulator (viva-cpm), be coupled to a genuine spatial
metabolism-and-diffusion simulator (spatio-flux) through nothing but a typed process interface,
and still show the same sense/act closure — now with real shape dynamics and real flux-balance
optimization behind it?

The flagship study, `cell-environment-coupling-spatial`, answers yes for this one pattern. One
coupling process, `CpmCellField`, is the entire interface: it reads the spatio-flux glucose
field at the CPM cell's current footprint, solves one dynamic-FBA step against `e_coli_core`
(oxygen-capped so the optimizer is pushed into mixed-acid acetate overflow, the way a real
glycolysis-outpacing-respiration cell would be), grows the CPM cell's target volume from the
biomass that solution produces, and writes the resulting uptake and secretion back into the
shared field as a spatial delta that spatio-flux's own diffusion process then spreads outward.
Over a 20-tick run the cell grows about 3.4-fold in CPM pixel volume, draws its own local
glucose down by close to a fifth before diffusion partially refills it, and leaves a spreading
acetate plume behind it — niche construction as a direct, unscripted consequence of two
independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

Three more patterns are built and run alongside it: multi-cell competition over a shared field
(`cell-cell-coupling-spatial`), a CPM structural-integrity collapse
(`disintegration-spatial`), and CPM growth-and-division (`growth-and-division-spatial`). The
rest — molecular-scale reaction-diffusion mechanisms, differential-adhesion sorting and phase
separation for complementarity, a self-maintained protocell for autopoiesis, colony
development-and-evolution, and the cellular-interface contract itself — are named in the
increment plan; some are planned, some in progress, not yet built. This investigation is honest
about being several studies deep into a nine-study plan, not finished.
question:
The companion investigation `draft-to-living-cell` specified the paper's nine
interface-composition patterns and ran them with toy-real, lumped mechanisms (ODEs, scripted
events, 1-D or 9-cell grids). This investigation asks whether the same patterns hold when the
environment is not a lumped store but a real 2D spatial field, and the cell is not a scalar
state bundle but a Cellular Potts Model (CPM) agent with genuine shape, footprint, and
motion. Concretely: does the Fig 5 sense/act loop survive being realized as a real CPM cell
(viva-cpm) sitting in a spatio-flux diffusing nutrient field, running dynamic flux-balance
analysis at its own footprint, growing, and secreting a metabolic byproduct back into the
field it depends on — composed from two independently-developed simulation frameworks through
one typed coupling interface (`CpmCellField`)?
hypothesis:
The paper's interface-composition patterns are not artifacts of the lumped,
low-dimensional mechanisms `draft-to-living-cell` used to demonstrate them — they hold when
the cell and its environment are realized in real 2D spatial frameworks built and validated
independently of this codebase (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes). One typed coupling process per pattern
(starting with `CpmCellField`, this investigation's flagship) is enough to compose those
frameworks without either one knowing about the other, and the resulting dynamics — nutrient
depletion, biomass growth, byproduct secretion and diffusion — are genuine simulation output,
not scripted. Across future increments, every one of the nine `draft-to-living-cell` studies
is expected to have a spatial counterpart; several are built and run so far (the flagship
cell-environment coupling, cell-cell coupling, disintegration, and growth-and-division), with
the rest planned or in progress.

executive.what_is_this:
This investigation is the spatial sibling of `draft-to-living-cell`. That
investigation turned the cellular-interface paper's nine composition patterns into inert
typed drafts compiled into small, lumped executables (ODE-scale mechanisms on 1-D or 9-cell
grids). This investigation asks the harder question: do those same patterns still compose
when the frameworks on each side of the interface are real, independently-built 2D spatial
simulators — a Cellular Potts Model (viva-cpm, a Rust-backed lattice engine with genuine cell
shape, adhesion, and volume dynamics) on one side, and spatio-flux's diffusion-advection PDE
solver plus dynamic flux-balance analysis on the other? Composing two frameworks that were
never designed with each other in mind is exactly the paper's central claim about typed
interfaces made concrete: `CpmCellField`, the flagship's coupling process, is the interface
where a CPM cell's footprint (a set of lattice pixels) is translated into a spatio-flux
field read, and where a dynamic-FBA solution (mmol/gDW/hr fluxes) is translated back into a
per-pixel field delta and a CPM target-volume update. Four studies are built and run so far —
`cell-environment-coupling-spatial` (the flagship, the spatial analogue of Fig 5's sense/act
loop), `cell-cell-coupling-spatial`, `disintegration-spatial`, and
`growth-and-division-spatial`. The remaining patterns from `draft-to-living-cell` (molecular
interfaces, biomolecular complementarity, autopoiesis, development-and-evolution, and the
cellular-interface contract itself) are named as future increments in the design spec; some
are planned, one (biomolecular complementarity) is in progress with code done but its study
not yet accepted.

The investigations are deliberate analogues, study-for-study, wherever the counterpart
exists: `cell-environment-coupling-spatial` here is the spatial realization of
`draft-to-living-cell/cell-environment-coupling`. Read them side by side — the lumped 9-cell
1-D executable there against the real 60x60 2D CPM+spatio-flux composite here — for the same
interface claim (sensing and acting are one coupling, not two subsystems; the cell measurably
reshapes the gradient it depends on) demonstrated at two very different levels of mechanistic
resolution.
executive.verdict:
Partial and honest: the flagship pattern holds. `cell-environment-coupling-spatial`
demonstrates that a real CPM cell, coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one
typed process (`CpmCellField`), closes the Fig 5 sense/act loop with genuine simulation
output — over 20 ticks the cell depletes local glucose (up to ~18% at its own footprint
before diffusion partially resupplies it), grows (CPM volume 32 -> 110 pixels, roughly 3.4x,
against a 3600-pixel lattice it does not come close to filling), and secretes acetate that
diffuses outward into a plume (`tests/test_flagship_field.py`, `tests/test_cpm_cell_field.py`,
`tests/test_cpm_viz.py`). This is niche construction as a real spatial and metabolic
consequence of coupling two independently-built simulators, not a scripted trajectory.

Three sibling studies are also built and run — `cell-cell-coupling-spatial` (competitive
exclusion and cross-feeding over a shared field), `disintegration-spatial` (a CPM
structural-integrity release), and `growth-and-division-spatial` (CPM growth and division
with partitioned daughter biomass). What this investigation has NOT yet shown is the
remaining patterns' spatial counterparts — reaction-diffusion molecular mechanisms,
differential-adhesion sorting and phase separation, a self-maintained protocell, colony
development, and the cellular-interface contract itself. Those are named in the design spec
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-cellular-interface-multicellular-design.md`) as the
increment plan; some are planned, others in progress. Chemotaxis toward the field (the cell moving up the gradient it
senses) is also deferred to a follow-up variant — the flagship cell's modest position drift
over the run is CPM thermal fluctuation, not directed motion.
decisions_needed: Four of the 9 planned spatial-counterpart studies are built and run so far — cell-environment-coupling-spatial (the flagship), cell-cell-coupling-spatial, disintegration-spatial, and growth-and-division-spatial. The remaining patterns — cellular-interface, molecular-interfaces, biomolecular-complementarity, autopoiesis, development-and-evolution — are named in the design spec's increment plan; some are planned, biomolecular-complementarity is in progress (code done, study.yaml held). Treat this investigation's verdict as scoped to the built studies only until the remaining increments land.

Chemotaxis toward the sensed field (directed up-gradient motion) is explicitly deferred to a follow-up variant of the flagship composite; the current flagship cell does not chemotax, only senses, metabolizes, grows, and secretes.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Composing a real 2D spatial cell-shape simulator (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts Model)
with a real spatial metabolism/diffusion simulator (spatio-flux's dynamic-FBA +
diffusion-advection) through one typed process interface reproduces the paper's Fig 5
sense/act coupling as genuine spatial, metabolic dynamics — not as a scripted or lumped
stand-in for it. The interface itself (`CpmCellField`) is the load-bearing artifact: it, not
either framework alone, is what makes the composition possible, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell`'s
central claim that a cellular interface is simultaneously a modeling choice and a testable
hypothesis about which interactions matter.
evidence_for:
cell-environment-coupling-spatial (the spatial Fig 5, this investigation's flagship) — a
real CPM cell reads a spatio-flux glucose field at its own footprint, runs one dynamic-FBA
step (`e_coli_core`, oxygen-capped to force acetate overflow), grows its CPM target volume
from the biomass produced, and writes uptake/secretion back into the field as a spatial
delta that `DiffusionAdvection` then spreads. Over 20 ticks: CPM volume grows ~3.4x (32 ->
110 px, ~3% of the 60x60 lattice — the cell does not fill it), local footprint glucose
depletes up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies it, and the field-wide acetate
total rises from 0 to ~47 (mmol-equivalent field units) as the secreted plume diffuses
outward. Net field-wide glucose falls (~32 of 5940 total field mass consumed) even though the
depletion signal is much sharper locally at the cell's own footprint than in the field-wide
total — the direct niche-construction signature.
evidence_against:
Five of the nine `draft-to-living-cell` patterns (molecular interfaces, biomolecular
complementarity, autopoiesis, development-and-evolution, and the cellular-interface contract
itself) have no spatial counterpart built and run yet — this investigation currently
demonstrates four patterns, not nine.

Chemotaxis (directed up-gradient motion) is deferred; the flagship cell senses and acts on
the field locally but does not move toward higher concentration.

The e_coli_core constants (`glucose_km`, `glucose_vmax`, `oxygen_vmax`, `box_volume_L`,
`grow_per_biomass`) are toy-real — plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to produce
gradual, spatially-legible dynamics over a short run, not fitted to any organism or medium.

The CPM lattice itself (the cell's shape, occupied pixels, footprint) lives inside
viva-cpm's Rust engine as a private, write-protected world object (`CpmCellField.world`),
not a process-bigraph store — only the coupling process reads and writes it. The
"environment" the interface exposes to the rest of the composite is exclusively the
spatio-flux `fields` store (glucose, acetate); the CPM's own internal field concept
(`field_at_cell`, `secretory_types`) is separate machinery this composite does not use.
caveats:
This investigation is still mid-buildout: four of nine planned studies are built and run
(the flagship plus cell-cell-coupling-spatial, disintegration-spatial, and
growth-and-division-spatial). The design spec
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-cellular-interface-multicellular-design.md`) lays out a
complete 9-study analogy to `draft-to-living-cell`; this file reflects the current increment,
not the finished plan.

Every mechanism here is toy-real: plausible constants, not calibrated to a named organism,
medium, or literature target. The dynamics demonstrate the coupling pattern (real spatial
sensing, metabolism, growth, secretion, diffusion), not a quantitatively validated cell.

Read alongside its specification-stage analogue,
`draft-to-living-cell/cell-environment-coupling`: that study closes the same Fig 5 loop over
a lumped 9-cell 1-D grid with a scripted-shape cell; this study closes it over a real 60x60
2D CPM cell with genuine shape and a real dynamic-FBA metabolism. Compare the two for the
same interface claim at two very different mechanistic resolutions.

studies.name: cell-environment-coupling-spatial
studies.title: Cell–Environment Coupling, Spatial (flagship)
studies.question:
Does the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense/act loop (Fig 5) hold as real spatial metabolism — one CPM cell sensing
a diffusing nutrient field, running flux-balance analysis at its own footprint, growing, and
secreting a byproduct back into the field — when the cell and its environment are each real,
independently-built simulators (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes) composed through one typed coupling process
(`CpmCellField`), rather than a scripted or lumped stand-in for that coupling?

findings.statement:
A real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
process (`CpmCellField`) closes the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense/act loop (Fig 5)
as genuine spatial metabolism: it
runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows both biologically (biomass) and structurally
(CPM lattice volume). Confirmed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37, CPM volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x) over
20 ticks, on a 3600-pixel lattice the cell occupies only ~3% of by the end.

The cell measurably depletes the local nutrient it senses before diffusion partially
resupplies it — niche construction as a direct spatial-metabolic consequence, not a scripted
trajectory. Confirmed: local footprint glucose concentration peaks at 1.15 (t=2) and falls to
0.94 by t=20, an up-to-~18% local drawdown, while the field-wide glucose total falls by only
~32 of 5940 units — the depletion signature is sharply local to the cell's own footprint and
its immediate diffusive neighborhood, not a field-wide event.

The O2-capped dynamic-FBA mechanism forces the optimizer into mixed-acid acetate
overflow (rather than pure aerobic respiration), and that byproduct genuinely diffuses
outward into a spreading plume via spatio-flux's own `DiffusionAdvection` process — the
secretion side of the coupling is as real as the uptake side. Confirmed: field-wide acetate
0 -> ~47.0 over 20 ticks.

studies.claim:
Composing a real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
coupling process (`CpmCellField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense/act
loop (Fig 5) as genuine spatial metabolism, not a scripted stand-in for it: over 20 ticks the
cell runs dynamic-FBA at its own
footprint (`e_coli_core`, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows ~3.4x in CPM volume (32
-> 110 px, ~3% of a 60x60 lattice it does not come close to filling), depletes local glucose by
up to ~18% before diffusion partially resupplies it (niche construction), and secretes a
diffusing acetate plume — two independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

biological_validation.basis: All four primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from a real 20-tick run — the cell metabolizes and grows (biomass, CPM volume), depletes its own local nutrient before diffusion resupplies it (niche construction), and secretes a diffusing acetate plume.

regression_compatibility.basis: single-cell-in-a-field.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the process-bigraph engine (tests/test_flagship_field.py, tests/test_cpm_cell_field.py, tests/test_cpm_viz.py); guarded skip when the optional cobra dependency is absent, matching draft-to-living-cell's FBA-grain convention.

explanatory_gain.basis: Composing a real Cellular Potts cell with a real spatial dFBA+diffusion simulator through one typed process makes the paper's sense/act-coupling claim concrete at a level of mechanistic resolution draft-to-living-cell's lumped 9-cell grid could not reach — genuine cell shape, genuine flux-balance optimization, genuine PDE diffusion, all talking through one interface neither framework was built with the other in mind for.

derived.insight:
A real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
process (`CpmCellField`) closes the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense/act loop (Fig 5)
as genuine spatial metabolism: it
runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows both biologically (biomass) and structurally
(CPM lattice volume). Confirmed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37, CPM volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x) over
20 ticks, on a 3600-pixel lattice the cell occupies only ~3% of by the end.

studies.name: cell-cell-coupling-spatial
studies.title: Cell–Cell Coupling, Spatial
studies.question:
Does the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated
figure) hold as real spatial multicellularity — multiple CPM cells sharing one diffusing
nutrient field, each running its own dynamic-FBA step at its own footprint, producing both
competitive exclusion and cross-feeding — when the whole colony is composed from independent
frameworks through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`), rather than the lumped
two-role, shared-scalar-pool stand-in `draft-to-living-cell`'s §Cell–cell coupling study used?

findings.statement: Multiple real CPM cells sharing one real spatio-flux nutrient field through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduce the paper's §Cell–cell coupling competitive-exclusion branch (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4), with each cell running its own independent dFBA solve at its own footprint on the same depleting field, drives a decisive biomass and lattice-volume split. Confirmed: biomass 237.9 vs 64.5 (3.69x), CPM volume 3511 vs 81 px, over a 20-tick run.

evidence.observed: biomass 237.9 (id 1) vs 64.5 (id 2); volume 3511 px (id 1) vs 81 px (id 2)

findings.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. Confirmed: consumer local_glucose 0.0, local_acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell.

The additive two-writer assumption `CpmColonyField`'s N-cell field update depends on -- that disjoint per-cell footprint deltas sum losslessly into one shared field -- is runtime-verified directly and independently of any dFBA mechanism, retiring what was previously an unverified assumption in the flagship study. Confirmed structurally: two synthetic single-pixel writers on disjoint pixels each apply independently and their combined effect exactly matches the sum of the two, over repeated ticks.

evidence.observed: two disjoint single-pixel writers each removing 1.0/tick over 3 ticks sum to a net field-wide change of exactly -6.0, with both individual pixels independently correct

studies.claim:
Composing N real CPM cells with one shared, real spatio-flux nutrient field through a
single N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–cell coupling
viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity, not a
scripted or lumped stand-in for it: over
20-tick runs, an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4) drives spatial
competitive exclusion (biomass 237.9 vs 64.5, a 3.69x margin; volume 3511 vs 81 px), while a
different composite over the same coupling process — a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing
acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming role — sustains a cell that never touches glucose
(local glucose 0.0) purely via a diffusing cross-feeding handoff (local acetate 1.30, biomass
1.25 -> 3.79). Both regimes run through the same process; only the composite's cell roles and
field constants differ, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell/cell-cell-coupling`'s law-4 pattern
(two handler environments negotiate the shared-resource constraint differently over one
interface) at real spatial, per-footprint metabolic resolution.

biological_validation.basis: All primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from real 20-tick runs -- the competition regime drives a decisive biomass/volume split between two otherwise-identical competitors differing only in uptake capacity, and the cross-feeding regime sustains a consumer cell that never touches glucose purely via a diffused acetate handoff. The foundational two-writer additivity control also passes, independent of both regimes.

regression_compatibility.basis: Both cellcell-compete.composite.json and cellcell-crossfeed.composite.json build and run to completion through the process-bigraph engine (tests/test_cellcell_regimes.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_field.py, tests/test_cpm_colony_viz.py); guarded skip when the optional cobra/cpm/spatio_flux dependencies are absent, matching this investigation's flagship and draft-to-living-cell's own FBA-grain convention.

explanatory_gain.basis: Generalizing the flagship's single-cell CpmCellField to an N-cell CpmColonyField and demonstrating both branches of the paper's §Cell–cell coupling viability-negotiation pattern (no dedicated figure) -- competitive exclusion AND cross-feeding -- from the same coupling process, differing only in the composite's cell roles and field constants, makes draft-to-living-cell's law-4 claim (different handlers over one interface negotiate a shared-resource constraint differently) concrete at real spatial, per-footprint dFBA resolution that its lumped two-role, shared- scalar-pool analogue could not reach.

derived.insight: Multiple real CPM cells sharing one real spatio-flux nutrient field through one N-cell coupling process (`CpmColonyField`) reproduce the paper's §Cell–cell coupling competitive-exclusion branch (no dedicated figure) as genuine spatial multicellularity: an uptake-capacity asymmetry alone (glucose_vmax 10 vs 4), with each cell running its own independent dFBA solve at its own footprint on the same depleting field, drives a decisive biomass and lattice-volume split. Confirmed: biomass 237.9 vs 64.5 (3.69x), CPM volume 3511 vs 81 px, over a 20-tick run.

studies.name: disintegration-spatial
studies.title: Disintegration, Spatial
studies.question:
Does the paper's §Disintegration level-shift (Fig 6) hold spatially -- a coherent CPM cell that loses structural
viability when a diffusing stressor field crosses its bound, its domain resorbing while its
shed material becomes scattering physical particles -- composed from independent frameworks
(viva-cpm + spatio-flux particles) through one coupling process (`CpmDisintegration` +
`BrownianMovement`)?

findings.statement:
A single real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux stressor field through one
coupling process (`CpmDisintegration`) reproduces the paper's §Disintegration level-shift
(Fig 6) as genuine spatial dissolution: the cell holds coherent while the diffusing stressor
field is below its
footprint-local viability bound, then latches a release once that bound is crossed at a
specific, deterministic tick, and its domain resorbs to full dissolution over the following
ticks. Confirmed: area > 30 through tick 6, released_tick == 7.0, area == 0 by tick 16, all
deterministic across repeated runs.

The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As the
domain resorbs, its vacated footprint pixels are converted into particles in a shared
map[particle] store, and that debris cloud keeps scattering (RMS spread strictly increasing)
well after the cell itself has fully dissolved, under a separate stock BrownianMovement
process. Confirmed: 68 particles shed by tick 16, RMS spread ~5.3 -> ~7.6 over an 8-tick
post-dissolution window.

The CPM-to-particle bridge this study's disintegration mechanism depends on --
that a process can emit particles via the map `_add` sentinel into a shared map[particle]
store, and a separate stock movement process can then move them -- is runtime-verified
directly and independently of the disintegration mechanism itself, retiring what was
previously an untested primitive. Confirmed structurally: a synthetic emitter's 3 particles
remain exactly 3 particles four ticks later, with at least 2 having moved under
BrownianMovement.

evidence.observed: 3 particles emitted, unchanged count 4 ticks later, >=2 moved

studies.claim:
Composing one real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux stressor field and a real spatio-flux
particle-movement process through two coupling processes (`CpmDisintegration` for the
viability-collapse trigger and resorption, stock `BrownianMovement` for the debris scatter)
reproduces the paper's §Disintegration level-shift (Fig 6) as genuine spatial dissolution, not a scripted or lumped
stand-in for it: over a deterministic 20-tick run, the cell holds coherent (area > 30) through
tick 6, the footprint-local stressor mean crosses viability_threshold at released_tick = 7, the
domain resorbs to area 0 by tick 16, and its 68 shed pixels become a debris cloud whose RMS
spread strictly increases through tick 24 -- hold, cross, resorb, scatter, end to end from one
coupling process plus one stock movement process, mirroring `draft-to-living-cell/disintegration`'s
§Disintegration level-shift pattern (Fig 6) at real spatial, per-pixel resolution.

biological_validation.basis: All primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from a real, deterministic 20-24 tick run -- the cell holds coherent, crosses its viability bound at a specific tick, resorbs to full dissolution, and sheds debris that keeps scattering after dissolution completes. The foundational particle-bridge control also passes, independent of the disintegration mechanism.

regression_compatibility.basis:
disintegration-spatial.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the
process-bigraph engine (tests/test_cpm_disintegration.py, tests/test_disintegration_regime.py,

studies.title: Growth and Division, Spatial
studies.question: Does the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b) hold spatially -- a CPM cell whose metabolism (dFBA solved at its own lattice footprint) grows its volume until it crosses a threshold and divides via the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` (mass-conserved), compounding into a small lineage over the run -- composed from independent frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) through one coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`)?

findings.statement: A single real CPM cell whose volume growth is driven by real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, coupled to the native CPM engine operation divide_cells through one process (CpmGrowthDivision), reproduces the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b) as genuine spatial compounding: the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase, reaching roughly 3-4 generations from a single seed cell, bounded by the shared glucose field and the lattice's finite capacity. studies.claim: Composing one real CPM cell, growing via real per-footprint dFBA metabolism, with the native CPM engine operation `divide_cells` through a single coupling process (`CpmGrowthDivision`) reproduces the paper's §Growth and division growth-then-divide pattern (Fig 10a,b) as genuine spatial multicellular compounding, not a scripted lineage or a lumped stand-in for it: over a 36-tick run sampled every 3 ticks, the population steps up in a monotonic non-decreasing staircase (1,2,2,2,4,4,5,8,8,11,14,18), spanning roughly 3-4 generations, while every cell's CPM volume stays bounded in a sawtooth between `reset_target` = 40 and `vol_threshold` = 80 -- growth, crossing, division, and resumed growth in the daughters, all as direct simulation output from three independently-developed frameworks (viva-cpm + spatio-flux + cobra) meeting at one typed interface. This mirrors `draft-to-living-cell/growth-and-division`'s §Growth and division claim (Fig 10a,b) (growth drives the cell's own state across a threshold; crossing the threshold triggers division) but realizes the division event itself as the native spatial CPM operation `divide_cells` acting directly on lattice pixels, in contrast to that study's place-graph rewrite (one node becoming two structurally-new nodes at a lumped, non-spatial level of composition).
